item.text:
**7B.9 | Sheikh Hasina (2024) research note**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is mostly negative for avoiding nepotism, favoritism, clientelism, and transactional politics. The best positive material is narrow and institutional, mainly procurement digitization and a partial cabinet refresh. I did not find reliable 2024 evidence on pardons/clemency specifically.

- **Sajeeb Wazed reappointed as PM’s ICT adviser** | **BSS** | **January 21, 2024** | [URL](https://www.bssnews.net/news-flash/169281) | Claim-level summary: Hasina reappointed her son Sajeeb Wazed as honorary ICT adviser. That is direct family-linked staffing and weighs against merit-neutral appointments. | **7B.9**
- **New Cabinet Formation: Loyalists, fresh faces likely to get priority** | **The Daily Star** | **January 9, 2024** | [URL](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/new-cabinet-formation-loyalists-fresh-faces-likely-get-priority-3515421) | Claim-level summary: contemporaneous reporting said the new cabinet would likely prioritize party loyalists, while technocrats would be rare. This is weak-to-moderate evidence of patronage-leaning appointment logic. | **7B.9**
- **Hasina springs cabinet surprises** | **The Daily Star** | **January 11, 2024** | [URL](https://online.thedailystar.net/election-2024/news/news/hasina-springs-cabinet-surprises-3516291) | Claim-level summary: Hasina dropped 30 old colleagues, brought in 15 new faces, and included two technocrats. This is the main counterweight on appointments, but it is still weak because the cabinet remained Awami League-centered and family-linked advisory posts remained in place. | **7B.9**
- **Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024) | Claim-level summary: Freedom House says corruption was endemic, anticorruption enforcement was politicized, media and civil society faced restrictions, and the Right to Information law was unevenly implemented. This is strong negative evidence for favoritism, selective enforcement, and limited transparency. | **7B.9**
- **Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) | Claim-level summary: Freedom House reports blocked news sites, throttled communications around BNP rallies, and later shutdowns during unrest. That is direct evidence against open access to public information and against neutral treatment of criticism. | **7B.9**
- **Bangladesh blocks roads and internet, deploys army to curb protests** | **Reuters** | **July 20, 2024** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) | Claim-level summary: Reuters reported soldiers in Dhaka, roadblocks, and internet/text shutdowns during the crackdown. This supports a finding of coercive enforcement and information suppression rather than neutral public administration. | **7B.9**
- **Bangladesh’s internet shutdown isolates citizens, disrupts business** | **Reuters** | **July 26, 2024** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladeshs-internet-shutdown-isolates-citizens-disrupts-business-3539448) | Claim-level summary: Reuters described a countrywide internet blackout during the protests and noted it had been used previously ahead of elections. This is strong evidence against transparent access to information and against restraint in enforcement. | **7B.9**
- **Purbachal plots: ACC to probe Hasina, family** | **The Daily Star** | **December 26, 2024** | [URL](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/crime-justice/news/purbachal-plots-acc-probe-hasina-family-3785406) | Claim-level summary: the Anti-Corruption Commission opened an investigation into alleged abuse of power in plot allocations to Hasina and close family members. Because this surfaced after her fall, it is retrospective rather than contemporaneous proof, but it is directly relevant to family favoritism and self-dealing. | **7B.9**

**Search gap**
- I ran targeted searches for 2024 pardons/clemency, family appointments, procurement reform, and information control. I found solid material on appointments, procurement, and censorship, but nothing reliable on pardons specifically. I would not infer a pardon pattern from absence of search hits.
- The positive side is mostly narrow and procedural: e-GP procurement reform exists, and the cabinet was not purely static. None of that offsets the stronger evidence of patronage, politicized enforcement, and information suppression.
